content.value_statement: Writing Hookify rules can be error-prone when events, patterns, and messages are unclear. This skill provides practical rule structure, examples, and workflow guidance for Claude-based automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains the markdown and YAML frontmatter format for Hookify rule files.
Documents bash, file, stop, prompt, and all event types.
Shows simple pattern rules and advanced multi-condition rule formats.
Provides regex writing tips for common Hookify matching needs.
Recommends file naming, storage, and gitignore practices for local rules.
Includes example rule messages for warnings, blocks, and completion checks.
limitations: It does not install Hookify or configure the runtime environment.
It does not validate regex patterns automatically inside the skill.
It provides guidance, not project-specific policy decisions.
It cannot guarantee that every generated rule matches all edge cases.

use_cases.title: Prevent risky shell commands
use_cases.description: Create rules that warn or block destructive Bash command patterns before Claude runs them.

use_cases.title: Review sensitive file edits
use_cases.description: Build file-event rules that warn when edits touch environment files, credentials, or key material.

use_cases.title: Enforce completion checks
use_cases.description: Write stop-event rules that remind agents to run tests, check builds, and update documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns when Claude tries to run a dangerous shell command. Explain each field briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Add file edit protection
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify file-event rule that warns when edits target environment files or credential names.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-condition rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule with multiple conditions for TypeScript files that add debug logging. Include a clear warning message.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and refine rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Hookify rule goals and propose precise event types, regex patterns, messages, and possible false positives.

output_examples.input: Warn when Claude adds console logging to production TypeScript files.
output_examples.output: A file-event rule plan with a TypeScript path condition, a console logging pattern, and a short warning message.

output_examples.input: Block destructive remove commands in Bash.
output_examples.output: A bash-event rule concept that matches recursive delete patterns and explains safer alternatives before command execution.

output_examples.input: Remind the agent to run tests before stopping.
output_examples.output: A stop-event checklist message that asks for tests, build status, and documentation review.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the risky behavior without blocking common safe work.
Write rule messages that explain the risk and give a clear next step.
Store local Hookify rules under the expected local file naming convention.
anti_patterns: Using broad patterns that match unrelated words or normal development commands.
Writing warning messages that only say no without explaining safer options.
Forgetting to test rules after changing patterns or event types.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create Hookify rule files that watch Claude actions and show warnings or blocks.

faq.question: Which Hookify events does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers bash, file, stop, prompt, and all event types.

faq.question: Can it create multi-condition rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains conditions with fields, operators, and patterns for more precise matching.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and guidance for writing rule files.

faq.question: Does it validate regex patterns?
faq.answer: No. It suggests testing patterns, but validation must happen in your environment.

faq.question: Can Codex and Claude Code use this guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude workflows and can guide Codex users who manage similar rule files.
